scope: THE JUMP TABLE: 13 handlers, one per mode; mode 4 reads a single -97 value, mode 3 an 11-bit value - so the modes select WHICH entity field is encoded

the_two_handlers_read_out.mode 3 at 0x6717A1: push 0xB ; call 0x66EC30 ; mov [esi+0x24], eax - reads an 11-BIT value into the scratch field at stream+0x24
the_two_handlers_read_out.mode 4 at 0x6717B5: mov eax,[ebp+8] ; mov ecx,esi ; call 0x66F9E0 ; mov [esi+0x28], eax - reads ONE value with the -97 codec (gate + 32 or gate + 8) into stream+0x28

what_this_means_for_the_payload: the mode does not enable a whole field list - it selects a SINGLE field and its codec
so an entity delta is: [mode selector][one field's value], repeated per changed field, and the changed bit at the start governs whether a delta is present at all
that is a completely different picture from the 'field table loop' the project assumed for entities, and it explains why entity payload experiments never lined up
the_practical_target: our entity currently decodes in mode 4, i.e. one -97 value, which lands in the stream scratch field at +0x28 rather than in the entity struct - so nothing visible changes yet
the interesting modes are the ones whose handlers write into the ENTITY struct (edi), not into the stream - reading 0x671890 / 0x671833 / 0x6718D2 will show which those are
one of them almost certainly writes eType, and another writes origin
next: read the remaining handlers 0x671890, 0x671833, 0x6718D2, 0x671979, 0x67193C and classify each by whether it writes [edi+...] (entity) or [esi+...] (stream scratch)
the handlers that write [edi+offset] are the ones that can put eType and origin into the entity
